summary: A native Android cache row larger than the ~2 MB CursorWindow (a file edit of a large file, a whole migrated legacy thread) failed the startup offline snapshot with SQLiteBlobTooBigException and left the machines list on 'Could not load machines'. Oversized cache rows are now dropped on open without being read, never written again, and skipped per row on read. Rows the user wrote (queued messages, drafts, pending actions, worktree requests) are never dropped: Room's queries skip an oversized one and it is read back in byte chunks, or quarantined in place if it cannot be decoded.

desktop.reason: The desktop reads better-sqlite3 in Node, which has no CursorWindow and no per-row size limit, and none of these Room tables exist there.

reactNativeIos.reason: CursorWindow is an Android framework limit; iOS SQLite and AsyncStorage reads have no per-row window, and the RN app does not use these Room tables.

sharedBackendApi.reason: Nothing on the wire changes; the backend still sends full file.edited contents and full lists, and only the phone's local cache is bounded.

automated: Robolectric (native SQLite, real CursorWindow) reproduces 'Row too big to fit into CursorWindow' with a 3 MB row, then shows the on-open repair drops it by size without reading it and startup yields the machines list
An unrepaired oversized cache row costs only that row in the offline snapshot; an unreadable cache table degrades to no cache

A 1600 KiB queued message and a 3 MiB multi-byte draft survive the repair and load through the offline snapshot, RoomOutboxStore and RoomComposerDraftStore; a user row that is not valid UTF-8 is quarantined and kept, never deleted

The cache deletes commit in their own transaction before any user-row scan; a scan that throws (in the head query or columnsOf) for one table is logged by table and exception class and skipped, leaving the cache rows deleted, the other tables recovered and startup unblocked
A legacy thread over the cap is not migrated and the migration still verifies and stays complete on the next run
Thread metadata over the cap deletes the older persisted snapshot and its feed rows, in a fake DAO and in real Room
Thread and browse cache stores never write a row over the cap and log sizes, never content
notExercised: Not run on the affected phone; the repair runs on the first launch of the next APK. No schema version change, so the Room upgrade path is unchanged.
